description: Demonstrator node for the shared _daycount.bundle.mjs kernel (SHARED-DAYCOUNT-BUNDLE-1): prices ONE caller-supplied date pair under ONE declared day-count mode and rolls both dates under the three business-day conventions. Nine closed modes. Seven are the _amort bundle's modes, extracted byte-compatibly (ISDA 2006 Definitions Section 4.16: 30_360_US, 30E_360, 30E_360_ISDA, ACT_360, ACT_365F, ACT_ACT_ISDA, plus the declared UNIT_PERIOD stub mode); two are new ids this bundle adds: ACT_ACT_ICMA (ICMA Rule 251 day count fraction over a caller-declared regular coupon-period schedule and compounding frequency 1, 2, 4 or 12) and BUS_252 (business days between the pair, over a caller-declared calendar, divided by the fixed 252). Every year fraction is returned as an exact gcd-reduced integer rational {num, den} so a caller rounds once after multiplying, plus a declared single-division float convenience value. Business-day rolls follow ISDA 2006 Definitions Section 4.12 (following, modified following, preceding) over caller data: weekend weekday numbers plus holiday dates supplied in policy_parameters and hash-pinned by the caller, never baked into kernel bytes (the _ruleversion single-writer ruling). Every out-of-domain input is a structured named refusal (unknown convention, bad or nonexistent date, inverted pair, missing or over-long schedule, bad frequency, missing calendar, unbounded roll), never a silent default. The bundle was differentially tested against the amortization bundle it was extracted from: 23,216,200 ordered date pairs spanning 1990-2060 with every month end and every Feb 28/29, zero mismatches at the amortization bundle's own declared 10-decimal half-up rounding (calendar modes agree to 1.4e-14 raw; the declared UNIT_PERIOD stub agrees within its declared 1e-9 scale). This node is shared machinery's demonstrator, not itself a wave-specific instrument: consumers inline the bundle directly per the composition contract rather than calling this node.
